newsitem.title: USA: Praxair extends energy saving efforts.
newsitem.headline: Praxair extends energy saving efforts.

text.p: Praxair Inc said Wednesday it has entered into one cooperative agreement and extended another with the U.S. Department of Energy to accelerate the commercialization of technologies that save energy and reduce emissions in metal-heating processes.
Praxair, DOE and other partner companies are committing about $2.5 million to fund the projects, the company said.

The cost-sharing agreements are for the continued development of Praxair's patented Dilute Oxygen Combustion technology, and for the commercial demonstration of the company's low-nitrogen oxide oxy-fuel combustion process.
Both advancements significantly reduce NOx and carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere, Praxair said.

Government environmental regulations restrict NOx emission levels, as they pose a potential health hazard and contribute to visible smog. Consequently, steel and aluminum producers are seeking cost-effective means to reduce emissions.
Praxair said its Dilute Oxygen Combustion and oxy-fuel combustion technologies will reduce NOx emissions by up to 95 percent.

The company said it estimates the use of oxy-fuel burners for steel reheating would increase oxygen consumption by at least 50 percent for most blast furnace-based steel producers. Similarly, oxygen consumption in electric-arc furnace-based mills would increase at least 100 percent.

Praxair is beginning Phase 2 of its Dilute Oxygen Combustion developmental efforts, working with two sub-contractors to bring the technology to near-commercial scale. North American Manufacturing Co is providing a pilot-scale test facility and Reaction Engineering International is supplying process modeling.
Praxair is working with Bethlehem Steel Corp and the State of Indiana to commercially demonstrate its low-NOx oxy-fuel combustion process for steel reheating.

The company said Bethlehem Steel plans to convert a furnace to Praxair's staged oxygen combustion system, which uses coke oven gas as fuel. Start-up of the furnace is scheduled for the first quarter of 1997.
